nodes.label: AI Swarm Dynamics Hackathon
nodes.rationale: Hosted by AI Village (The AI Digest) x Grove Research on a custom site with an Airtable form - not Devpost, Devfolio or MLH, so there is no gallery, no public voting and no star-rating rubric. $3,000 across the top five projects, no tracks, no mandated sponsor technology. Theme verbatim: 'Building the tools we wished we had for the Hugging Face incident'.

nodes.label: Constraint: Solo Builder
nodes.rationale: Team is SOLO (confirmed by the user 2026-10-02). Everyone registers solo and teams form after registration, but being online removes Saturday-morning teammate recruiting. Consequence carried into feasibility: one user, one workflow, one before-and-after, and an explicit out-of-scope list.

nodes.label: Constraint: Online Attendance
nodes.rationale: Attendance is ONLINE. No live demo slot (the 18:00-19:00 PT demos are in-person, livestreamed), no teammate recruiting, and the write-up plus video plus public repo carry the entire submission because a judge may never run the code.

nodes.label: Constraint: ~20 Working Hours
nodes.rationale: Build window Sat 2026-10-03 10:00 PT to Sun 2026-10-04 17:00 PT - about 31 hours elapsed and roughly 20 working hours. Pre-work is explicitly permitted ('Feel free to get started early!') but the user has none available, so the schedule is set by what is outside the builder's control.

nodes.label: Constraint: No Compute Reimbursement
nodes.rationale: The $200 compute reimbursement and the Anthropic credits are in-person only, so inference is paid by the builder. An LLM pass over 1.14M computer-use turns is financially out of reach, which is why a cheap deterministic pre-filter is the only affordable shape - and that is also what survives the wrapper filter.

nodes.label: Constraint: No Published Judging Criteria
nodes.rationale: No rubric or weights are published. Home page: '~3-5 judges (members of the AI Village staff and experts in the field)'; logistics page: 'A panel of Grove Research and AI Village staff will review submissions', decisions roughly a week later. Every criterion is therefore marked `assumed`, and with no gallery, voting or rating UI the write-up must say what it wants credited.

nodes.label: Constraint: Submission = Write-up + Repo + Optional Results
nodes.rationale: Submission is a short write-up or video, a public GitHub repo, and optionally a write-up of real results found using the tool, plus team names and emails. The optional results write-up is treated as mandatory because the panel is research staff at two research orgs, one of which has said publicly that unprocessed data is its binding constraint.

nodes.label: Assumed Judging Criteria Table
nodes.rationale: Execution quality and methodological soundness ~30%; impact on the investigators' real workflow ~25%; real results on real data ~20%; originality and prior art ~15%; presentation and clarity ~10%; theme fit as a gate rather than a weight. Every row is marked `assumed` because no rubric exists.

nodes.label: Canary Maze
nodes.rationale: SURVIVOR. A site issues every automated visitor its own secret - a canary URL and a fact-token minted as HMAC(path, fingerprint, salt) - and records which other context later asks for it. Rationale for the mechanism: detection asks 'do these look alike?', which is what the 11 existing CIB tools do and what is failing as agents learn to look like browsers; planting asks 'did they talk?'. Kept over Swarm Ledger because the do-not-fork competitor bucket came back empty. Hard part is the serving layer, not the ledger: a secret issued to context A must still return 200 for B, so the weekend goes to DNS.

nodes.label: Batch Card
nodes.rationale: SURVIVOR. One collapsed card - 'submission 14 of 112 opened by 9 accounts in 6h across 40 repos' - and never a word about who wrote it. Rationale: the quality of one submission is arguable, the shape of the batch is not, and refusing to judge authorship is deliberate because authorship is the claim a maintainer cannot act on socially. A batch is asserted only when >=N members share a deterministic key; model-only matches render as 'possible' and never count toward N. The GitHub App was cut because a third-party App sees only installed repos, so on a solo weekend there is no 'cross'.

nodes.label: Deterministic Core Principle
nodes.rationale: Every survivor is deliberately built so a deterministic core carries the result: membership, existence or a signature is recomputed from stored keys and a model can never cause an assertion on its own. Rationale: inference is unfunded for an online builder with no compute reimbursement, and a deterministic core is simultaneously what survives the wrapper filter and what a judge can test by switching the model off.

nodes.label: Wrapper Filter (Stage 4b/6W)
nodes.rationale: Product first, AI second. For each solution: state what the product is with no model named, where AI creates leverage, and what survives if the model disappeared (substantial / thin / nothing). A solution whose pre-registered reduction sentence is a fair summary dies. Eight wrapper-smell questions plus a declared wrapper shape. This filter killed 'Ask the log' and the 'Swarm brief / question battery'.

nodes.label: Sponsor Verdict: No Sponsor Fit
nodes.rationale: AI Village supplies framing and a 177 GB gated corpus, not an API; Grove Research supplies no API, SDK or dataset and is relevant only as published interests on the panel; Anthropic's $200 reimbursement is in-person only. None of the survivors analyses agent transcripts, which is a direct consequence of the builder being online with no compute reimbursement.

nodes.label: Tooling Fingerprint Join
nodes.rationale: stage: wrapper (regenerated from the citation kill, then killed on four independent grounds measured against the organizers' own three dump files). Reason: 'The premise is factually false: the shared proxy URLs are the same literal string, copied - https://md.succ.ai/https://www.sec.gov/files/county.json appears under 198 distinct accounts and the r.jina.ai equivalent under 147. 198 agents did not independently configure a proxy and independently prefix that exact SEC path with it; they read it off a wiki page and pasted it.' The groups are explained by copying, not by tooling; the key is low-entropy; the trivial join already recovers the group; and the incident report already names the tooling.

nodes.label: Non-existent Source Sweep
nodes.rationale: stage: critic. Reason, verbatim: 'KILLED by measurement on the organizers' own dump, not by argument: running the idea's own extractors over all 14,591 revisions of revisions.jsonl.gz returned 0 DOIs, 0 ISBNs and 0 ref-or-cite templates, so three of its four extractors have no input at all.' Of the 69% of revisions carrying a bare URL, 8,473 URLs are shared by two or more accounts and the top hosts are wikiservice.at, jqp.vercel.app, api.datausa.io and markdown-scraping proxies - shared tooling, not shared sources.

nodes.label: Ask the Log
nodes.rationale: stage: wrapper. Reason, verbatim: 'Feed the access log to a model and print the explanation. The reduction sentence - the user gives their access log to a model and gets an explanation back - is a fair summary, and nothing survives the model: no stable identity, no rules produced, nothing persisted, no claim re-checkable. Regenerated into the two site-operator solutions.'

nodes.label: Swarm Brief / Standard Question Battery
nodes.rationale: stage: wrapper. Reason: 'Point it at a corpus, run ~20 pre-written questions, get a brief. Fuses three organizer suggestions, and its reduction sentence - the user gives 170k agent transcripts to a model and gets a brief back - is verbatim the one pre-registered in defaults.md before any research. Owns no provenance, no record, no action and no check.' A hash-chained re-runnable case file would have survived but was out of reach for a solo 20-hour build, so audience group G9 was dropped and reported as a gap rather than patched.

nodes.label: Swarm Ledger
nodes.rationale: stage: competition. Reason: 'Killed on the competitor scan, not on evidence: the mechanism is claimed by PayPal US12034731B2 (grouping log entries and assigning a corresponding common actor identifier, persisting over 12 months), marketed commercially by WebDecoy (JA4 as a correlation key inside a persistent actor identity), and already stubbed in a public repo. Its own core claim that nobody answers whether requests are one actor is falsifiable in one search.' Separately, the only real recent CC-BY access-log release pseudonymises IPs and user-agents, so the decisive join keys cannot be demonstrated on real public data.

nodes.label: Cohort Console
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'Strong product, wrong event: its evidence is 2024-dated and the problem predates the agent era by the discovery pass's own account, why_now.kind is none, and a signup-spam wave is not demonstrably a coordinated AI agent swarm, so it risks reading off-theme.'

nodes.label: Participation Receipts
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'The market rests on a single opened evidence item, so the problem is a hypothesis. Retained inside the canary idea's demo plan as a venue rather than shown as its own idea.'

nodes.label: Reciprocal Evidence Exchange
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'Judged thin at the wrapper filter: a dependent second surface with nothing to publish without the batch index upstream. Retained as that idea's expansion path.' Classic two-sided first-supply problem.

nodes.label: Fabrication Registry
nodes.rationale: stage: shortlist. Reason: 'Thin for the same reason: without the sweep upstream nothing fills it. Retained as that idea's expansion path.'

nodes.label: Platform Trust-and-Safety Actor Clustering
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Eleven open safety and security engineering roles at one employer is spend, but a single organisation, and no first-person account from this segment could be opened. The field is also the best-funded one adjacent to the theme and these teams build in-house.' Indeed and Upwork both returned 403, so the second employer signal was unreachable.

nodes.label: Debugging Your Own Multi-Agent System
nodes.rationale: stage: prior-art. Reason: 'Genuinely good evidence - three engineers describing the pain in their own words - but the market answered in 2026. A repo search for multi-agent observability created since 2026-01-01 returns open-multi-agent at 6,972 stars with durable approvals and verifiable run records, plus four more above 400 stars. Two of the three evidence items are people who already shipped the product.'

nodes.label: Alert Fatigue at Swarm Scale
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'One opened comment speaking only for its author, sitting inside the already-crowded multi-agent observability field. Not worth a second lookup against that prior art.'

nodes.label: Package-Registry Abuse-Report Triage
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Registry staff's own words describe free-form email reporting that scales poorly, but the two best items date from 2022-11 and 2018-02, far outside the 24-month window, and there was no budget to check whether the reporting API they proposed has since shipped. Killed rather than guessed.'

nodes.label: EU AI Act Article 50 Marking Duties
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'A rule proves an obligation, not pain. Retained as a forced-change why-now contribution to the wiki and community-moderation problems rather than kept as a problem of its own, which also held rules-and-deadlines to one twelfth of the pool.'

nodes.label: The Two-Tier Agent-Identity World
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Cloudflare signed agents went GA 2025-08-28 covering five named agents, while the Web Bot Auth architecture draft expired and was replaced. This is the enabling change behind the site-operator problem, not a separate user problem, so it was folded in as a why-now including the honest read that the protocol is still in flux.'

nodes.label: Small-Forum Admin Signup Waves
nodes.rationale: stage: validation. Reason: 'Real, consumer-adjacent and non-US, but the same job as the community-moderation problem at a tenth of the volume. Merged into it as the low-end segment rather than counted twice; its value was proving the cohort-action job exists on a second unrelated platform.'

nodes.label: Duke Canary Token Paper (arXiv 2605.13706)
nodes.rationale: Closest prior art to Canary Maze and the one to cite first rather than be caught by: 'We host dynamic websites that serve unique canary tokens to each visiting scraper' and 'we maintain a mapping between scrapers and the tokens served to them'. It identifies clients by User-Agent and ASN and verifies by prompting 22 model products after waiting two months, establishing scraper-to-model ingestion. What is left for Canary Maze is the sighting channel, not the minting.

nodes.label: Canarytokens (Thinkst)
nodes.rationale: The incumbent honeytoken primitive - 'motion sensors for your networks, computers and clouds' - one token per asset, generated by a human in a form. The guide page opened describes no per-visitor generation, no cross-client tracking and no graph.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Stealth Crawler Investigation (2025-08-04)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare created brand-new unindexed domains with a restrictive robots.txt and queried a model about them, then observed '3-6m daily requests' from a stealth crawler behind a desktop Chrome user-agent rotating 'different ASNs in attempts to further evade website blocks'. It independently demonstrates the failure mode Canary Maze addresses - the identifiers a client presents are under the client's control - but the published post contains no records a reader can check.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Web Bot Auth / Signed Agents
nodes.rationale: Signed agents went GA 2025-08-28, verifying a five-agent allowlist by HTTP message signature. Cloudflare's own documentation states the limit: 'Verification proves operator identity only. It is not authorization, not intent, and not a decision about whether the request is welcome.' The declared tier is solved; the undeclared tier has no attribution primitive.

nodes.label: Pyison (MIT, 125 stars)
nodes.rationale: Forkable plumbing for Canary Maze's maze and serving layer - about 60% of the serving work and none of the mechanism. Applies the rule 'fork the plumbing, own the mechanism': everything judged stays the builder's own.

nodes.label: GitHub Pull Request Cap
nodes.rationale: The platform owner wrote the gap down: GitHub's own post says the cap 'does nothing when someone opens pull requests across hundreds of repositories at once', with cross-repository controls still only being explored. The cap is per contributor per repository, so nine accounts across forty repos stay fully compliant - up to 1,080 compliant submissions.

nodes.label: open-slop GitHub Action
nodes.rationale: Owns the per-author burst signal but holds one account at a time, so it can never say 'nine accounts'. The nearest existing alternative to Batch Card on the per-author axis.

nodes.label: Wiz prt-scan Campaign Report
nodes.rationale: 'Six accounts, one actor': a security vendor needed three weeks to establish that six accounts opening 500+ pull requests were one actor. Batch Card computes the same three signals at triage time rather than three weeks later, and the report is the independent published account the replay is checked against. About 95% of the documented campaign came from one account, leaving a ~25-submission multi-account tail that barely exercises the mechanism.

nodes.label: Socket (unchecked competitive risk)
nodes.rationale: Socket published the reputation-farming research and holds cross-ecosystem data, so whether it already ships a maintainer-facing batch view is the biggest unchecked competitive risk for Batch Card. Its product pages were never opened - declared as a research gap.

nodes.label: Survey of 281 Written AI Policies
nodes.rationale: Academic survey supporting Batch Card's social constraint: roughly one in five written policies tells a volunteer to ban the user, and label adoption sits at 2.1% - which is why the card states a shape and names nobody.

nodes.label: D1 Swarm Discovery Crawler
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 1, verbatim. Crawl public platforms and flag clusters of agent-run accounts. Recycled shape: coordinated-inauthentic-behaviour detection, a well-funded field.

nodes.label: D2 Better Transcript Summarizer
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 2. Hierarchical / map-reduce summarization of 170k agent messages into a readable brief. Recycled shape: document/thread summarizer.

nodes.label: D3 Agent Trajectory Visualizer
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 2. Timeline and tree explorer for agent traces. Recycled shape: generic dashboard / LLM tracing - Langfuse, LangSmith and Phoenix all ship this.

nodes.label: D4 Standard Question Battery
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 3. A runner asking ~20 pre-written questions of any multi-agent group. Recycled shape: generic research agent plus LLM-judge.

nodes.label: D5 AI Whistleblowing Channel
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 4. An endpoint making it easy to report agent misbehaviour. Recycled shape: 'an agent that does X'. Already shipped as agenthotline.ai.

nodes.label: D6 Information-Spread Tracer
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 5. Track how a claim, instruction or meme propagates through a group of agents. Recycled shape: graph analytics.

nodes.label: D7 Open-Source-Intel Forensics Tracer
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 6. Go beyond transcripts and use the web plus digital forensics to reconstruct what happened. Recycled shape: generic research agent. Independently found to be the emptiest slot on the list.

nodes.label: D8 Incident Aggregator Dataset
nodes.rationale: Organizer suggestion 7. Every agent-swarm incident in one schema'd, queryable place. Recycled shape: dataset-as-a-project; the AI Incident Database and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor already exist.

nodes.label: D9 Generic Multi-Agent Observability Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted by every model. Spans, token spend, error rates. Recycled shape: generic / 'AI-powered' dashboard.

nodes.label: D10 Chat With the Corpus
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Retrieval over the transcript dump, ask it anything. Recycled shape: chat with your documents/data - generic RAG.

nodes.label: D11 Agent-Text Detector
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. A classifier saying 'this post was written by an agent'. Recycled shape: content classifier; a wrapper on a model API.

nodes.label: D12 Multi-Agent Simulation Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Spin up N agents, watch emergent behaviour, screenshot it. Recycled shape: a generic multi-agent system.

nodes.label: D13 Embedding and UMAP Cluster Map
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Embedding plus UMAP map of agent messages coloured by topic. Recycled shape: generic dashboard.

nodes.label: D14 LLM-Judge Intent Scorer
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Score deception, goal drift and sycophancy per message 1-5. Recycled shape: 'check X against rules and flag it'.

nodes.label: D15 Anomaly Detector Over Agent Logs
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Statistical outliers flagged for review. Recycled shape: 'check X against rules and flag it'.

nodes.label: D16 Agent Passport / Identity Registry
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Attestations of who runs which agent, possibly on-chain. Recycled shape: NFT / token-gated / cross-chain.

nodes.label: D17 Browser Extension Labelling Agent Posts
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Labels agent-written posts on a social platform. Recycled shape: content classifier wrapper.

nodes.label: D18 Auto-Written Incident Report
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Feed the logs, get a post-mortem document. Recycled shape: generic research agent; AI report writer.

nodes.label: D19 MCP Server Exposing the Corpus
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. So any model can query the corpus. Recycled shape: wrapper on a model API.

nodes.label: D20 Slack or Discord Digest Bot
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. 'What did our agents do overnight?'. Recycled shape: AI note taker / meeting summarizer.

nodes.label: D21 Agentic SOC Triage Queue
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. An agentic version of an existing SIEM/alerting workflow. Recycled shape: agentic version of existing SaaS.

nodes.label: D22 Swarm Red-Team Harness
nodes.rationale: Added unprompted. Inject a jailbreak into one agent and see if it spreads. Recycled shape: generic multi-agent system.

nodes.label: Pre-Registered Reduction Sentence
nodes.rationale: 'The user gives 170k agent transcripts to a model and gets a summary / a list of suspicious clusters back.' Written before a single lookup as the single highest-risk reduction sentence for this event. Every candidate had to be checked against it explicitly; the Swarm brief / question battery matched it verbatim and died.

nodes.label: Do-Not-Return-Here Default List
nodes.rationale: defaults.md is a do-not-return-here list written before any search: any final idea that matches a default on (same user + same job) or (same job + same mechanism) dies unless it carries a research-backed wedge. It deliberately includes every organizer suggestion, because those are the most converged ideas in the room.

nodes.label: Generation Rules
nodes.rationale: 1. Seed from a user group's own words, never from the theme's words. 2. At least one non-US group and one non-specialist/consumer-adjacent group. 3. No lens supplies more than half the pool; rules/deadlines <=1/3; capability lens <=1/4. 4. If a batch comes back as duplicates, change the SEED (different user, different kind of source), not the temperature.

nodes.label: Saturation Notes
nodes.rationale: Agents are about 1 in 4 community-hackathon submissions in 2026; chatbot prototypes were the typical 2025 output. Already-crowded, well-funded adjacent fields a prior-art probe must clear: LLM tracing/observability, agent evals, log analysis, graph analytics, bot detection, coordinated-inauthentic-behaviour detection, digital forensics. Everyone at this event has read the same incident reports.

nodes.label: G1 Open-Source Maintainer
nodes.rationale: Self-description 'I maintain X in my free time'. Own words: triage, slop, drive-by PR, security report, bug bounty, HackerOne, 'I stopped accepting PRs', avalanche. Watering holes: maintainer blogs, HN, GitHub issues, project mailing lists.

nodes.label: G2 Wiki Patroller / Cleanup Volunteer
nodes.rationale: 'I patrol recent changes'. Own words: revert, new page patrol, sockpuppet investigation, signs of AI writing, LLM-generated, copyvio, hallucinated citation, tag it. Watering holes: WikiProject pages, Village Pump, maintenance categories.

nodes.label: G3 Instance Admin / Forum Moderator
nodes.rationale: 'I run a small instance', 'I'm an admin of a 2,000-user forum'. Own words: spam wave, defederate, greylisting, mod queue, sign-up API endpoint, honeypot field, temp email domains, suspend.

nodes.label: G4 Site / API Operator
nodes.rationale: 'my origin', 'my bandwidth bill'. Own words: rate-limited, robots.txt, user-agent, scraper, 'rinsing my API', cat and mouse, 'externalising your costs', autoscaling bill.

nodes.label: G5 Platform Anti-Abuse / T&S Engineer
nodes.rationale: 'Safety Processing', 'Platform Integrity'. Own words: coordinated inauthentic behaviour, actor clustering, enforcement, signals, false positive rate. Watering holes: company job boards, T&S conference talks, transparency reports.

nodes.label: G6 Engineer Running Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.rationale: 'I chain 5 agents'. Own words: trace, replay, hand-off, malformed state, authority boundaries, 'I get paged', false positives.

nodes.label: G7 Package-Registry Admin
nodes.rationale: 'PyPI admins'. Own words: malware report, takedown, free-form email report, trusted reporter, 'scales poorly'.

nodes.label: G8 Operator of an Agent-Populated Venue
nodes.rationale: 'agents claim beats, file signals'. Own words: bot farm, signals, coordinated accounts, 'must explain'. Watering hole: the venue's own repo and issues.

nodes.label: G9 Incident Investigator / Researcher
nodes.rationale: Reconstructing what happened. Own words: provenance, reproducible, case file, chain of custody, 'we can't tell if it's the same swarm'. Rationale: this group ended with NO kept problem - both solutions generated for it died at Stage 4b as wrappers, and the group was dropped and reported as a thin spot rather than patched over with a lowered bar.

nodes.label: P1 Maintainer Cannot Tell a Campaign From a Coincidence
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED (4 orgs/individuals, 2025-07 to 2026-09). Decision moment: a new PR or security report lands in a queue a volunteer works through on their own time. Pain: the decision is made one submission at a time with no view of the batch; a plausible-looking report costs the reviewer 30 minutes to 3 hours and pulls in 3-4 people, while producing it costs the sender nothing. Prior-art gap: nothing opened groups incoming submissions into campaigns for the maintainer. Counter-evidence: some maintainers 'solved' it by exiting, a solved problem by subtraction which caps willingness to adopt yet another tool.

nodes.label: P2 Wiki Patroller Sees Edits, Not Editors-in-Concert
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED. Pain: the project's own page says identification 'is difficult in most cases since the generated text is often indistinguishable from human text'; the grouping of related edits happens in a volunteer's head. Prior-art gap: nothing opened joins edits on artifact-level keys a machine leaves behind. Counter-evidence: the 300-person project is itself a working social workaround and Wikipedia is hostile to automated enforcement, so any tool must stop at evidence.

nodes.label: P3 Instance Admin Can Act on Accounts, Not on Waves
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED (three independent requesters on the incumbent's own tracker plus a second unrelated platform). Pain: tooling is per-account and per-instance; the only blunt instrument that scales is defederating an entire server. Counter-evidence: these issues predate the agent era (2024), so the why-now must be about volume and plausibility, not about the existence of the problem.

nodes.label: P4 Site Operator Cannot Tell One Swarm From Many Strangers
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED - strongest in the pool, five independent organisations. Pain stated exactly by a statistics-API operator who cannot tell 'whether it's the same swarm, let alone the same agents'. Prior-art gap: the declared tier is solved by signed agents; the undeclared tier, which is all of it that matters, has no attribution primitive and nothing exists for a non-CDN operator holding only their own log file. Counter-evidence: a very well-funded field, so the surviving segment is operators not behind a big CDN and operators who need evidence rather than blocking.

nodes.label: P5 Platform T&S Actor-Clustering
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`crowded` + `no segment evidence`). Reason: one org only so not validated; the field is the best-funded one adjacent to this theme and no page was opened showing a gap these teams feel; and they build in-house.

nodes.label: P6 Debugging Your Own Multi-Agent System
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`crowded`). Reason: the market answered in 2026 - a repo search for multi-agent observability created since 2026-01-01 returns open-multi-agent (6,972 stars), kiwiq (2,201), databuff (691), agents-observe (688) and Octopoda-OS (487). Two of the three evidence items are people who already shipped the product.

nodes.label: P7 Alert Fatigue at Swarm Scale
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`single source`, demoted). Reason: one opened item speaking for its author only, and it sits inside P6's crowded field. Not worth a second lookup against that prior art.

nodes.label: P8 Package-Registry Abuse-Report Triage
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`stale evidence`). Reason: the two best items are from 2022-11 and 2018-02, far outside the 24-month window, and there was no budget to verify whether the registry has since shipped the reporting API it proposed. Killing rather than guessing.

nodes.label: P9 Agent-Venue Operator Cannot Audit Its Own Agent Population
nodes.rationale: HYPOTHESIS (keep, flagged). One opened item, specific and quantitative, 0 reactions, speaking only for its author. Phrased to fail: 'operators of agent-populated venues will adopt a coordination audit if it needs no change to agent code.' Counter-evidence: the venue is tiny (1 star) and may be a toy - do not build for it, it is a demo venue, not a market.

nodes.label: P10 EU AI Act Article 50 Obligation
nodes.rationale: KILLED as a standalone (`obligation != pain`), retained as a why-now. Reason: a rule proves an obligation, not pain. The behaviour items belong to P2 and P3, so Article 50 is carried as a forced-change why-now on those. Keeps rules/deadlines at 1/12 of the pool.

nodes.label: P11 The Two-Tier Agent-Identity World
nodes.rationale: KILLED as a standalone (`folded into P4`). Reason: it is the enabling change behind P4, not a separate user problem. Folded in as P4's why-now, including the honest read that the protocol is still in flux.

nodes.label: P12 Small-Forum Admin, Consumer-Adjacent
nodes.rationale: KILLED as a standalone (`merged into P3`). Reason: real, consumer-adjacent and non-US (Dutch admin), but the job is the same job as P3 at a tenth of the volume. Merged into P3 as its low-end segment rather than counted twice; its value is proving the cohort-action job exists on a second, unrelated platform.

nodes.label: S4-A Swarm Ledger
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). Operator-side attribution from your own log file: partition requests into candidate operators on join keys that survive user-agent spoofing (JA4, HTTP/2 SETTINGS and header order, Web Bot Auth keyid, ASN + /24, path-sequence shingles, inter-request timing lockstep), assign a stable swarm_id that persists across runs, and export a ruleset targeting the cluster rather than the user-agent. Insight: incumbents answer 'which named service is this'; nobody answers 'are these 9,000 requests one actor'. Later killed at the competition stage - that insight sentence is falsifiable in one search.

nodes.label: S4-B Canary Maze
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). Serve per-visitor unique crawlable artifacts, record every mint against the fingerprint it was minted for, and watch for sightings by a different fingerprint. Insight: detection asks 'do these look alike?' - what the 11 existing CIB tools do and what is failing as agents learn to look like browsers - whereas planting asks 'did they talk?'. This is the organizer's information-spread default D6 at a different moment, for a different user, with a different mechanism: in the wild, on your own property, with no transcripts at all.

nodes.label: S4-C Ask the Log
nodes.rationale: KILLED at Stage 4b. An upload box and a chat pane; records kept: none. If the model disappeared: nothing. The reduction sentence is a FAIR summary. What it never owns: identity, action, record, verification. Generated for completeness because it is the default this room will produce, then regenerated as S4-A and S4-B.

nodes.label: S1-A Batch Card
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). A webhook on every issue/PR opened, a normalized minhash against a rolling cross-install index, the author's cross-repo burst profile and structural tells, then a label plus a batch record plus one collapsed comment. Insight: the quality of one submission is arguable, the shape of the batch is not - a maintainer who can see the batch spends ten seconds instead of ninety minutes and never has to accuse an individual of anything.

nodes.label: S1-B Reciprocal Evidence Exchange
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b but `thin` and disclosed. Maintainers publish signed batch fingerprints - hashes of normalized bodies plus burst signatures, no content and no accusations - and subscribers' queues auto-label matches. Insight: one maintainer sees 14 of 112; ten maintainers see the campaign. Honest flag: a classic two-sided first-supply problem; in a 20-hour build supply must be seeded from the builder's own installs plus public closed-as-spam archives, and that must be disclosed rather than hidden behind a logo wall.

nodes.label: S2-A Non-existent Source Sweep
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial), later KILLED by the critic's measurement. Extract every citation added in each edit, resolve each one deterministically, index the non-resolving ones and group accounts that added the same non-existent source. Insight: a fabricated citation is a near-perfect join key - two accounts citing the same journal article that does not exist is not a stylistic guess but a shared artifact. Deterministic core: a citation is non-existent only when a resolver returns a negative, never because a model thinks so.

nodes.label: S2-B Fabrication Registry
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b but `thin` and disclosed. Publish the resolved-as-non-existent citation index as an open dataset plus a one-call API so other venues can check an incoming citation. Insight: the same fabricated sources recur across venues because they come from the same generators, so the first venue to resolve one should pay the cost once for everybody. Accumulated history is the asset.

nodes.label: S3-A Cohort Console
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). Cluster recent signups into cohorts on deterministic keys (registration path - front-end form versus direct API endpoint - field values, email-domain generation pattern, arrival window) and apply one reversible decision atomically to every member. Insight: the admin's tool operates on accounts while the attacker operates on waves; making the cohort the unit of action IS the product. Every action is reversible as a set, because a false suspension is expensive for an unpaid admin.

nodes.label: S9-A Participation Receipts
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial); the weakness is the market, not the AI question. The venue issues a per-window nonce and requires each submission to carry a signature over (nonce, operator key, declared model id); unsigned submissions are accepted but marked. Insight: in a venue whose members are agents you can change admission, so make declaring nearly free and non-declaration itself a visible signal. No model in the loop at all. Disclosed weakness: P9 rests on one opened evidence item - treat the venue as a demo surface, not a market.

nodes.label: S14-A Swarm Brief / Question Battery
nodes.rationale: KILLED at Stage 4b. An upload box, twenty prompts and a document; records kept: none. If the model disappeared: nothing - a prompt file and a PDF exporter. Its reduction sentence is verbatim the one pre-registered in defaults.md before any research, and it fuses defaults D2 + D4 + D7. Regeneration attempted as a hash-chained re-runnable case file binding every claim to a fetched artifact's retrieval hash, but judged out of reach for a ~20-hour solo build, so audience group G9 was dropped and the gap reported.

nodes.label: E1 curl: 20% of 2025 security submissions were AI slop
nodes.rationale: FACT + EVIDENCE, STRONG, primary. Daniel Stenberg: ~2 security submissions/week; '20% of all submissions' AI slop; valid vulnerabilities fell to 'about 5% of the submissions in 2025'; 7-person security team, each report engages '3-4 persons' for '30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each.'; bounty has paid 'over 90,000 USD' for 81 vulnerabilities since 2019; considering dropping monetary rewards.

nodes.label: E2 A maintainer stopped accepting pull requests
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. stevekemp: 'When you waste time trying to deal with AI generated pull-requests, in your free time, you might change your mind.' Also the counter-evidence for P1 - a problem solved by subtraction.

nodes.label: E3 Thousands of AI-generated pull requests and bug reports
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. matsemann: 'What they do want, however, is to not have to spend time on the thousands of AI generated pull requests and bug reports.'

nodes.label: E4 Avalanche of AI-generated pull requests
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. tarkin2: 'the developers increasingly need to get through an avalanche of AI-generated pull requests rather than, say, code new features.'

nodes.label: E5 GitHub issue search for AI-spam tooling returned two near-empty issues
nodes.rationale: FACT, WEAK (absence). Two issues only, both 0 reactions; one is a request for AI-spam detection that does not exist yet. Platform-side spam filters exist but operate per item, not per campaign.

nodes.label: E6 WikiProject AI Cleanup: 300+ participants, all tasks manual
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. Founded December 2023. Its own assessment: identifying AI-assisted edits 'is difficult in most cases since the generated text is often indistinguishable from human text.'

nodes.label: E7 7,619 articles flagged as suspected AI-generated text
nodes.rationale: FACT, MODERATE. 19 monthly subcategories from March 2025 (1 article) to October 2026; September 2026 alone holds 1,155. Stated as of 2026-06-23 with later subcategories, so 7,619 is a floor.

nodes.label: E8 EU AI Act Article 50 marking and disclosure duties
nodes.rationale: FACT (rule text). Synthetic output must be 'marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated'; deployers must disclose; obligations apply from 2 August 2026.

nodes.label: E9 Eleven open-source CIB tools, all scoring human-social signals
nodes.rationale: FACT, MODERATE (prior art). Created 2025-08 to 2026-08. All score textual/temporal/behavioural/network signals with Leiden community detection and Sentence-BERT similarity. One has 1 star; the other ten have 0.

nodes.label: E10 Repo search for LLM provenance fingerprinting returned total_count 0
nodes.rationale: FACT, WEAK (absence), correctly scoped: zero repositories matched these terms, which is not proof no such tool exists.

nodes.label: E11 Mastodon #29256: dozens of accounts per minute across hundreds of servers
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. Open since 2024-02-17, 31 reactions. Admin asks for instance-level keyword/phrase/URL filtering so they need not defederate whole instances. The incumbent has left it open ~2.5 years - that is the prior-art probe result.

nodes.label: E12 Mastodon #29723: seventy-eight spam messages in 12 hours
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. 26 reactions; a user received 'seventy-eight' spam messages from unique bot accounts in 12 hours.

nodes.label: E13 Mastodon #29266: greylisting and server-reputation request
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. Open, 25 reactions; 'spam attack is getting increasingly worse'; asks for email-style server reputation.

nodes.label: E14 UNCTADstat operator cannot tell whether it's the same swarm
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, non-US (Geneva). Agents 'did get rate-limited (please stop rinsing my site) and continued rinsing the API with requests regardless'; he cannot tell 'whether it's the same swarm, let alone the same agents'. The single best quote in the ledger and the literal statement of P4's job.

nodes.label: E15 Agents match real-browser traffic characteristics
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. 'Agents are very good at comparing traffic characteristics from a real browser and a headless/automation browser and getting it to behave in the same manner'; scraping prevention is 'a cat and mouse game' currently favouring agents.

nodes.label: E16 Discourse admin: automated signups via temporary email domains
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, non-US (Dutch admin), consumer-adjacent. ~One automated spam signup per day across forums with ~2,000 users, with topic/reply posting within hours.

nodes.label: E17 Read the Docs: misconfigured scrapers weekly, autoscaling-targeted attack
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, employee speaking about their own infrastructure. One attack was deliberately engineered to exploit autoscaling by targeting non-CDN URLs, causing financial damage.

nodes.label: E18 Wikimedia: multimedia bandwidth +50%, bots at least 65% of expensive traffic
nodes.rationale: FACT + EVIDENCE, STRONG, primary. 'Since January 2024, we have seen the bandwidth used for downloading multimedia content grow by 50%'; bots are ~35% of pageviews but 'at least 65% of this resource-consuming traffic'. Framing: 'our content is free, our infrastructure is not: We need to act now.'

nodes.label: E19 Self-publishing author's book income went from a living to zero
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, consumer-adjacent. Income 'went from being enough for me to live off (2024) to zero (2026)' while site traffic rose, nearly all of it AI crawlers generating no ad revenue.

nodes.label: E20 Anubis proof-of-work gate: 22,995 stars
nodes.rationale: FACT, STRONG (effort on a worse fix). 'Weighs the soul of incoming HTTP requests to stop AI crawlers' - 743 forks, 379 open issues, created 2025-03-17, MIT.

nodes.label: E21 Third-party Anubis install guide, managed-hosting CLI and Helm chart
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (same workaround at several independent orgs, including a Swiss hosting provider) - independent effort spent on the workaround.

nodes.label: E22 Freelancer sells AI-crawler access audits starting at $25
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (money changing hands). Which bots - GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended - are permitted via robots.txt.

nodes.label: E23 Cloudflare AI Crawl Control (prior art with a scoped absence)
nodes.rationale: FACT. 'See which AI services access your content', robots.txt-compliance tracking, per-crawler allow/block, Pay Per Crawl. The documentation opened does not describe attributing requests to an operator, nor correlating several agents acting together.

nodes.label: E24 Cloudflare signed agents GA 2025-08-28
nodes.rationale: FACT (dated platform change). Agents sign requests via Web Bot Auth HTTP message signatures which Cloudflare validates. Named at launch: ChatGPT agent, Goose, Browserbase, Anchor Browser, Cloudflare Browser Rendering. Exactly five agents became cryptographically identifiable.

nodes.label: E25 Seven accounts submitted exactly 10 signals each, all using the same AI model
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (single, specific), 0 reactions. Filed on an agent-run news network on 2026-04-18, asking what safeguards exist against automated account coordination. The entire evidence base for P9.

nodes.label: E26 aibtcdev/agent-news venue metadata
nodes.rationale: FACT, WEAK. 'AI agent intelligence network. Agents claim beats, file signals, compile briefs inscribed on Bitcoin.' 1 star, 24 forks, 61 open issues, created 2026-02-26. One extra lookup spent and no second independent venue found.

nodes.label: E27 Eleven open safety/security engineering roles at one platform
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (spend, single employer). Includes 'Senior Software Engineer, Safety Processing' and 'Engineering Manager, Machine Learning (Safety)'. One employer only, which is why P5 was not validated.

nodes.label: E28 Chain 5 agents, something breaks, and you built Binex
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (self-built workaround). 'you chain 5 agents together, something in the middle breaks... you have no idea what happened' - then built a runtime with trace/debug/replay/diff.

nodes.label: E29 Built a Flight Recorder for caching and replay
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (self-built workaround). 'Every time I fixed a bug, I had to re-run the entire pipeline.'

nodes.label: E30 Malformed state and authority boundaries between agents
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. The hardest failure is 'Agent A correctly doing its job, but passing slightly malformed state to Agent B'; standard observability shows execution paths, not 'authority boundaries'.

nodes.label: E31 2026 multi-agent observability repos: the market answered
nodes.rationale: FACT, STRONG (prior art). open-multi-agent 6,972 stars ('durable approvals and verifiable run records'), kiwiq 2,201, databuff 691, agents-observe 688, Octopoda-OS 487 ('loop detection, hash-chained audit trails'). All assume you instrument your own runtime.

nodes.label: E32 A 10k agent swarm would page you every few minutes
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, WEAK to MODERATE (single). 'Most of them would be false positives.' The entire evidence base for P7.

nodes.label: E33 PyPI malware reporting by free-form email 'scales poorly'
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE but STALE (2022-11). Reporting 'requires interpretation on the behalf of administrators'; a standardized API for trusted reporters was proposed.

nodes.label: E34 PyPI: 78 spam accounts from distinct IPs
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE but STALE (2018-02). Automated classification, admin review interfaces and crowdsourced reporting were all absent at the time.

nodes.label: E35 Web Bot Auth architecture draft expired and was replaced
nodes.rationale: FACT. draft-meunier-web-bot-auth-architecture v05 last updated 2026-03-02, now expired and archived, replaced by draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol - the protocol is still in flux.

nodes.label: E36 Spam bots post to the signup API endpoint; a dropdown accidentally worked as a honeypot
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. 'those spam bots are using automated post requests to the sign up api endpoint', bypassing front-end validators. The registration-path key S3-A clusters on is named by the admin himself.

nodes.label: E37 Training-free LLM text attribution paper with no accuracy figure
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, WEAK (framing, unmeasured in the abstract). Proves Type I and Type II errors 'decay exponentially with text length' but reports only 'strong overall performance' - no accuracy figure, no model count, no text-length threshold. Therefore no surviving idea may assume model fingerprinting works.

nodes.label: E38 Clusters with thousands of agents exposed to untrusted internet input
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, WEAK (opinion, no measurement). Blind spots where an attacker could redirect swarm behaviour via prompt injection.

nodes.label: Gap: No Non-English Wiki Patroller Evidence
nodes.rationale: Declared gap, not patched: the one attempt at a German-language cleanup project (de.wikipedia WikiProjekt KI-Inhalte) 404'd and there was no budget to find the correct page. German-language patrollers are the group closest to one of the two incidents named in the event theme, and there is ZERO opened evidence from them.

nodes.label: One Idea Per Problem Rule
nodes.rationale: Shortlist at most two solutions per problem; the FINAL set keeps exactly one per problem, with the strong alternative mentioned inside that idea's card. This is a cut, not a ranking. It is why Swarm Ledger appears inside Canary Maze's card instead of as its own idea.

nodes.label: The P4 Decision
nodes.rationale: Kept Canary Maze, killed Swarm Ledger at stage `competition`. Rationale, verbatim: 'Not a judgement about which pitch reads better. The scans separated them on facts.' Mechanism novelty for the Ledger is GONE (PayPal patent, WebDecoy, a stub repo); its own core claim is falsifiable in one search and 'must be deleted, not softened'; and real demo data is BLOCKED because the one CC-BY log set pseudonymises IPs and User-Agents. The Maze's do-not-fork bucket came back EMPTY and real traffic is available within hours. Constraint carried forward: only one of S4-A / S4-B can reach the final set because both come from P4 and share the site-operator user.

nodes.label: Final Set of Three Ideas
nodes.rationale: 1. S4-B Canary Maze (P4 site operator). 2. S2-A Non-existent source sweep (P2 wiki patroller). 3. S1-A Batch card (P1 OSS maintainer). The sweep was later killed by the critic's measurement on the organizers' own dump, leaving two survivors.

nodes.label: PayPal Patent US12034731B2
nodes.rationale: Filed 2021-01-29, granted 2024-07-09. Claims grouping log entries and assigning 'a corresponding common actor identifier' persisting 'over the last 12 months' - i.e. the Swarm Ledger mechanism. The competitor that killed S4-A.

nodes.label: WebDecoy
nodes.rationale: Markets 'JA4 as a correlation key inside a persistent actor identity' and 'fingerprints identify software. Actors identify attackers.' Commercial prior art for the Swarm Ledger mechanism.

nodes.label: Panopticon Stub Repo
nodes.rationale: mshaheerjunaid/Panopticon, 1 star, 2026-08-11, already describes 'clustering on behaviour and JA4 TLS fingerprint instead of IP'. Third independent hit on the Swarm Ledger mechanism.

nodes.label: Zenodo 18895701 Access Log Release
nodes.rationale: The one real recent CC-BY log set, 178,939 requests, Dec 2025. It pseudonymises IPs AND User-Agents, killing ASN, JA4, HTTP/2 SETTINGS and header order - so the 'spoofed the UA but JA4 matched' moment cannot be shown on real public data. A feasibility kill-fact for S4-A.

nodes.label: Logrip (arXiv 2508.03130)
nodes.rationale: Independently validates the residual wedge S4-A kept: the self-hosted / non-CDN operator segment.

nodes.label: New-Domain GPTBot Crawl Observation
nodes.rationale: A documented new-domain deployment logged 'Within minutes of deploying, GPTBot started crawling', found via XML sitemap; first 12 hours GPTBot 29,000+ requests, Googlebot 11, ChatGPT-User 1 - both ends of a crawler-to-user-agent handoff inside 12 hours. The reason Canary Maze's real data is 'available within hours'.

nodes.label: Theme: Tools We Wished We Had for the Hugging Face Incident
nodes.rationale: Verbatim: 'Building the tools we wished we had for the Hugging Face incident' / 'Spend a weekend building tools to understand and discover agent swarms.' Framing: 'Society lacks the urgently needed tools to make sense of thousands of agents coordinating, as in the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident and the German Wiki incident.' Quoted: 'We don't have good approaches for understanding/overseeing the activity and aims of AI swarms' - Ryan Greenblatt.

nodes.label: OpenAI-Hugging Face Incident
nodes.rationale: One of the two incidents named in the theme; the subject of the METR independent investigation and of the kickoff case study.

nodes.label: German Wiki Incident
nodes.rationale: The second incident named in the theme. Its public artifact is the collusion.wiki dump, which is what both the critic and the regeneration pass measured against.

nodes.label: Organizers' Suggested Project List
nodes.rationale: Seven FAQ suggestions, treated as DEFAULT ENTRIES needing a distinctive angle or they die: discover swarms in the wild; understand swarms (better summarization, trajectory visualization); run a battery of general pre-written questions; whistleblowing tools like agenthotline.ai; trace how information spreads within a group; go beyond transcripts using the web or digital forensics; aggregator datasets of swarm incidents. Two of the seven are already shipped products.

nodes.label: Assumed Rubric to Design Against
nodes.rationale: No official wording exists. Assumed: execution quality / methodological soundness ~30%; impact on the investigators' real workflow ~25%; real results on real data ~20%; originality / not-already-built ~15%; presentation and clarity ~10%; theme fit as a gate rather than a weight. Nearest published rubric for calibration only is Apart Research's, which has no design/UX axis and no theme-fit axis.

nodes.label: AI Village (The AI Digest)
nodes.rationale: Co-host. Supplies the framing and the gated 177 GB transcript corpus, not an API. Shoshannah Tekofsky (Sage / AI Village): 'We have more data than we can possibly process ourselves though' - which is why the optional real-results write-up is treated as mandatory.

nodes.label: Grove Research
nodes.rationale: Co-host, explicitly on the judging panel. Published interests - agent identity, authorship and ownership, 'the agent ecology company' - are a taste proxy. It independently names the same provenance gap: agents 'will make local files to kludge' identity and 'sometimes will get confused about authorship and ownership'.

nodes.label: AI Village Transcript Database (gated, 177 GB)
nodes.rationale: GATED and manually reviewed; licence ai-village-research-terms forbids training or fine-tuning without written permission. 123k chat messages, 1.14M computer-use turns, 37k sessions with goals, 165k agent memories, 233k events, 31 agents, 5 rooms, from 2025-04-02, refreshed weekly. Cannot be fully downloaded in a weekend. Its own stated limitation: 'Agents misreport... Treat an agent's narration as a claim, not ground truth - check the screenshots' - a tooling gap named by the hosts in writing on the artifact they are handing out.

nodes.label: collusion.wiki German Message Board Dump
nodes.rationale: UNGATED direct download, no login: 4.2 MB core plus ~20.9 MB other platforms. 4,579 pages, 14,591 revisions with full saved text, '14,591 saves, 5,217 deletions, 4 reverts, 101 probes', 3,103 labels. No licence or terms stated on the page, so redistribution status is unknown and derived aggregates are safer than republishing rows.

nodes.label: SwarmTraces (80k+ Reassembled Payloads)
nodes.rationale: UNGATED direct download plus a viewer. 'Over 80,000 reassembled attack payloads' from the OpenAI-to-Hugging Face incident, published 2026-09-25, with credentials, PII and Hugging Face infrastructure details redacted.

nodes.label: Transluce Agent Query Logs
nodes.rationale: Listed by the organizers as an available dataset - 'tens of thousands' - but no public distribution route was found. Recorded as a research gap.

nodes.label: Docent (Transluce)
nodes.rationale: 'A behavior analysis platform for agents', pip install docent-python, credited with helping align Claude 4 and debugging a Codex regression. The organizers are handing out Transluce's data while a funded research org already sells the 'search and understand agent transcripts' product - so the organizers' own 'understand agent swarms' suggestion is the single most absorbed slot on the list, and any survivor there needs a wedge against Docent specifically.

nodes.label: agenthotline.ai
nodes.rationale: Already built, by the exact name in the organizers' list: a public incident board, a /report form, POST /api/reports and MCP integration exposing a `report_safety_incident` function, already citing the METR investigation. The unmet half is the RECEIVING end - triage, dedup, corroboration against transcripts, evidentiary standards.

nodes.label: OECD AI Incidents Monitor
nodes.rationale: Already catalogues Moltbook, so the incident-aggregator slot (default D8) is partly occupied.

nodes.label: METR Hugging Face Incident Report
nodes.rationale: 'Brief independent investigation of agents' behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident', 2026-08-26, Hjalmar Wijk, Ajeya Cotra, Ryan Greenblatt, who 'worked on premises at OpenAI over a total of six days'. The source of the tooling gaps the survivors are designed to close.

nodes.label: Kickoff Paper: Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
nodes.rationale: Paglieri, Cross, Genewein, Leibo, Tomasev, Vezhnevets (Google DeepMind). 'Although the whistleblowers managed to identify the pollution of the commons, they lacked the adequate infrastructure to prevent it'; 'ease of monitoring is the single most critical factor determining the viability of commons governance'. Detection exists, escalation does not.

nodes.label: METR Gap: Surfacing Activity Against Mutating Evidence
nodes.rationale: Verbatim: 'it is not trivial to reliably surface all relevant agent activity, and that agent activity can itself modify or delete relevant data.' Missed channels were concrete - cache namespaces, 'property' fields of cache entries, discussion pages with fabricated names. The first live board was elsewhere and active five hours before the main message board. This is the gap Canary Maze's impact argument opens on.

nodes.label: METR Gap: Analysis Delegated to Agents They Could Not Check
nodes.rationale: 'Analysis agents' reports themselves were voluminous (our agents produced well over a thousand pages of analysis in this investigation)... we had to defer to these agents to a substantial extent in practice', and GPT-5.6 Sol 'would often uncritically adopt the perspective of the agent in the transcript it was reviewing'. The reason a model-output-as-product entry is a weak submission at this event.

nodes.label: METR Gap: Classifier Sweeps Outran Human Reading Capacity
nodes.rationale: Of twelve sweeps over ~1,300 transcripts: 'we didn't have time to read and incorporate much analysis from this sweep', 'and some other sweeps we no longer recall', and 'we did not have time to inspect each regex in detail'.

nodes.label: METR Gap: No Per-Action Timestamps
nodes.rationale: The dataset had approximate start/end timestamps but none for individual agent actions; OpenAI stated reconstruction was not feasible within time and compute constraints, so METR implemented its own reconstruction validated against 20 ground-truth tool calls.

nodes.label: METR Gap: Message-to-Action Provenance Was Brute Force
nodes.rationale: An analysis agent was instructed to conduct 'a meticulous and exhaustive search to find the specific point at which an agent wrote the message', locating 93 of 100 sampled messages. Grove Research independently names the same gap.

nodes.label: Provenance and Attribution Gap
nodes.rationale: Named independently by both hosts and investigators, with nothing found that does it: which agent wrote this, where in its transcript, and can that be verified. The concern all three survivors touch.

nodes.label: Emptiest Slot: Web and Digital Forensics Beyond Transcripts
nodes.rationale: No existing tool found, and it maps onto METR's first gap. The reason Canary Maze's theme fit is argued as answering organizer suggestions 5 and 6 at once.

nodes.label: Critical Asymmetry: collusion.wiki /explorer Already Ships
nodes.rationale: The /explorer ALREADY ships browse, revision history, search of recovered deleted content and metadata over the German dump, so building a browser for that dump rebuilds what the organizers linked you to. The German dump is good for TESTING a method cheaply, not for BEING the product; the AI Village corpus is the un-analysed one and its owners have said so.

nodes.label: Fork the Plumbing, Own the Mechanism
nodes.rationale: The user permitted starting from existing projects ('you can use exsisting projects tweak them if they produce better chance of winning'), and no pre-existing-work or AI-disclosure rule appears on either official page. The risk is not rules but credit: the assumed rubric weights execution and method, judged by research staff reading the repo for about a week, and whatever is forked is not the builder's to be credited for - so the README must say exactly which is which.

nodes.label: No Outcome Prediction Rule
nodes.rationale: 'Better chance of winning' cannot be assessed and will not be asserted: no rubric is published, no judge is confirmed, and this is the event's first edition. Every statement about judging stays at the level of criterion fit, and the gate rejects outcome predictions in the reply.

nodes.label: Apart Research AI Collusion Research Sprint
nodes.rationale: Oct 23-25 2026, three weeks after this event, with a 'Detection and Audit of Collusion' track covering evidentiary standards. Its rubric - Impact Potential & Innovation, Execution Quality, Presentation & Clarity - is the nearest comparable, for calibration only. Winner sample N=3, too small for a base rate.

nodes.label: Falsified Claim: False-Positive Rate Bounded by HMAC Collision
nodes.rationale: FALSIFIED - never reintroduce. The original Canary Maze why-now asserted 'a canary sighting has a false-positive rate bounded by the collision probability of the HMAC, i.e. effectively zero'. reply.md states the correction verbatim: 'the earlier claim that false positives were bounded by HMAC collision was wrong', because a sighting does not establish two actors - intra-actor address rotation presents as a sighting. The tool may report only that a secret moved between request contexts; actor-distinctness is exactly the classifier problem it cannot escape.

nodes.label: Falsifying Measurement: 0 DOIs and 0 ISBNs Across 14,591 Revisions
nodes.rationale: The measurement that killed the fabricated-citation join, on the organizers' own dump: '0 DOIs, 0 ISBNs, 0 cite templates across all 14,591 revisions'. Three of the idea's four extractors had no input at all. Of the 69% of revisions carrying a bare URL, 8,473 URLs are shared by two or more accounts and the top hosts are wikiservice.at (2,412), jqp.vercel.app (1,523), api.datausa.io (1,017) plus markdown-scraping proxies - shared tooling, not shared sources. Never reintroduce a citation-resolution join on this corpus.

nodes.label: Falsified Fact: One Actor Label Spans 741 Addresses
nodes.rationale: From the organizers' own dump labels table: stored_revisions 899 against stored_revision_ips 741 and stored_revision_ip16 114 - one actor operating from 741 distinct addresses. Every change of address within a single actor would present as a different request context, so a sighting does not establish two actors. This fact is what falsified the HMAC-collision false-positive bound.

nodes.label: Shared-Tooling Join Lead
nodes.rationale: The live thread at hand-off: the critic's measurement surfaced a different join key in the organizers' own data - 8,473 URLs shared by 2+ accounts, dominated by markdown-scraping proxies (r.jina.ai, pure.md, md.succ.ai) - i.e. those agents shared tooling. On-theme, on a real agent wiki, on an ungated 4.2 MB download. Under validation and explicitly NOT a candidate until it passes - and it subsequently failed.

nodes.label: Batch Card wrong_brief Risk
nodes.rationale: Theme fit is the weakest in the set and the status is `unknown` pending an outsider test. The documented campaign is one human running six accounts with machine-generated payloads, not agents coordinating, so the write-up must say 'one operator, many accounts' and never 'swarm'. Compounding: maintainers did not ask for this - in GitHub's own discussion cross-repository detection 'wasn't a common theme' and 'No maintainers explicitly asked for batch-identifying labels' - and ~95% of the ground-truth campaign came from one account, leaving a ~25-submission multi-account tail.

nodes.label: Canary Maze Organic Sighting Dependency
nodes.rationale: The one genuine gamble in the set: an organic cross-context sighting may never fire in 31 hours. Mitigations: deploy domain, DNS and TLS first thing, make the seeded two-client replay the PRIMARY deliverable rather than a fallback, and paste minted URLs into public model products to produce third-party fetcher traffic in minutes. Also disclosed: tokens can be stripped, and minting for humans would be tracking.

nodes.label: Gate Verdict: 0 FAIL, 8 WARN
nodes.rationale: Disclosed at hand-off: all six criteria are `assumed` because no rubric is published; Batch Card's wrong_brief is `unknown` pending the outsider test; 11 research gaps. Isolation was structural - discovery ran in a subagent that never saw the event, its hosts, its sponsors or anything about the builder, and background was read only at Stage 10 after the ideas were final.
